text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 8.1% today, continuing a sharp two-week slide that has cut the stock nearly 16% lower. The most concrete trigger appears to be the company's quarterly earnings announcement and report filed on November 3rd—two days before today's decline accelerated. While the data doesn't specify what disappointed in those results, the timing lines up with the stock's steepest fall (from $430 on November 3rd to $392 today), suggesting investors reacted negatively to the company's disclosed numbers or forward outlook.

The broader context adds pressure: oil refining margins have tightened as US crude prices sit at $99.64 per barrel while refineries operate at 94.5% capacity, and storage levels for both oil and refined products remain elevated. This combination typically compresses the profit spread refiners make on turning crude into gasoline and diesel—a structural headwind independent of any single quarter's results.
